objective: Define the governed Primary / Backup Provider Strategy for market data, context data, macro/on-chain sources and future execution venues without selecting final production providers.
scope: Define domain-specific primary, backup and authoritative cross-check roles
Define independence requirements so backup paths do not share the same failure domain where avoidable
Define health, divergence, failover, degraded and recovery states
Define data-provider failover separately from execution-venue failover
Define conditional candidate pools using P01-B/C evidence
Carry P01-D jurisdiction/client-class restrictions into candidate eligibility
Carry P01-E licensing/data-rights/cost constraints into candidate eligibility
out_of_scope: Select the final production provider, broker or exchange
Purchase subscriptions or accept vendor contracts
Open accounts, KYC, create credentials or fund accounts
Implement data adapters or execution adapters
Enable Demo, Shadow, Live or Auto Trading
tests: Every domain has explicit primary/backup/cross-check semantics or an explicit reason why not
Backup paths are evaluated for failure-domain independence
Execution failover is not treated as equivalent to data failover
No candidate with unresolved jurisdiction or required data-rights status is marked production-selected
No final production provider, broker or exchange is selected
security_tests: No automatic live broker failover authorization
rollback: Revert P01-F strategy artifacts and state/catalog reconciliation only. No runtime/provider/account changes are made.
definition_of_done: Failover and recovery states are documented
Task Catalog and Current State are reconciled
